headline: BARRICK SHATTERS Q1 ESTIMATES: $1.21B Free Cash Flow, EPS Up 256% on 719,000 oz at $4,823 Gold
snippet: Barrick Mining reported Q1 2026 attributable EPS of $0.96, up 256% year-over-year, with $1.21 billion in attributable free cash flow on 719,000 oz of gold at a $4,823 realized price. Revenue reached $5.22 billion and the company beat its own production guidance of 640,000–680,000 oz, buoyed by Nevada Gold Mines and a resumption at Loulo-Gounkoto ahead of its planned North American IPO.

headline: SILVER SPIKES 6%+: $85.85 Spot as Sixth Consecutive Annual Supply Deficit Deepens
snippet: Silver spot surged more than 6% on May 11 to $85.85/oz as a projected sixth-straight annual supply shortfall of 46.3 million ounces collided with safe-haven flows from the U.S.-Iran conflict and structural industrial buying from solar manufacturing and AI data centre buildouts. Above-ground silver stocks have fallen over 762 million ounces since 2021.

headline: BRUNSWICK DRILLS 17.7m at 1.10% Li2O Within 123m Corridor at Quebec Anatacau Project
snippet: Brunswick Exploration (CSE: BRW) intersected 17.7 metres at 1.10% Li2O within a 123-metre continuous interval averaging 0.72% Li2O at its Anatacau Main Project in Quebec's James Bay, extending the mineralized corridor beyond 500 metres. The company also reported the highest-grade cesium intercepts in the James Bay region — up to 11.8m at 1.84% Cs2O — adding a critical mineral co-product dimension to the project.

headline: Wallbridge Expands Dragonfly Corridor: 4.53 g/t Au Over 13.5m in First 2026 Martiniere Holes
snippet: Wallbridge Mining (TSX: WM) released results from the first two holes of its 17,000-metre 2026 Phase 1 campaign at Martiniere, returning intercepts up to 4.53 g/t Au over 13.5m and 3.11 g/t Au over 18.4m along the Dragonfly corridor. Four Phase 1 holes remain pending assay, with management describing the system as open both laterally and at depth.

headline: HONEY BADGER SURGES 63%: Prairie Creek Acquisition Closes, High-Grade Germanium Identified
snippet: Honey Badger Silver (TSXV: TUF) jumped 63% in a week after closing its acquisition of Canadian Zinc, taking 100% ownership of the Prairie Creek silver project in the NWT — one of Canada's largest undeveloped silver deposits — for C$10 million plus 12.5 million units. The company immediately followed with a research partnership announcement revealing high-grade germanium potential at Prairie Creek.

headline: ZERO SHIPMENTS: China Acid Ban Leaves Chile's Copper Producers Without Sulphuric Acid
snippet: Chinese sulphuric acid shipments to Chile — critical for heap-leach copper processing — hit zero in March 2026 as Beijing's outright export ban took effect from May, threatening roughly 20% of global copper output that depends on acid-intensive SX-EW processing. Acid spot prices in Chile have doubled in seven weeks to $380/mt, with no near-term alternative supply in sight.

headline: Chile Lithium Exports SURGE 175%: SQM-Codelco Partnership Drives Record April Shipments
snippet: Chile's lithium carbonate exports reached $498 million in April 2026, up 175.6% year-over-year, as the SQM-Codelco government partnership ramps output ahead of schedule. Q1 lithium carbonate revenues of $1.108 billion are up 147.7% YoY — now eclipsing copper as Chile's highest-value export category.

headline: SACRIFICE ZONES: Critical Minerals Rush Leaves Toxic Legacy as AI and Clean Energy Demand Spikes
snippet: An investigation documents how the race to mine rare earths, lithium, and other critical minerals for AI infrastructure and clean energy is creating environmental sacrifice zones that disproportionately affect poor rural communities — even as tech companies and governments tout climate goals. The piece argues demand projections are outpacing any realistic mitigation framework.

headline: NdPr CRASHES 21% in April to $99.61/kg — Western Producers Hold; June MIIT Quota the Next Catalyst
snippet: NdPr oxide fell 21.0% in April to $99.61/kg — its sharpest monthly decline since the Q1 rally — but remains 88% above its January opening price and well above the operational cost base of MP Materials and Lynas. Prices are expected to consolidate in a $95–$115/kg domestic range through Q2 2026, with China's mid-year MIIT mining quota announcement in June as the next major directional catalyst.

headline: Uranium Spot Pushes Above $100/lb: AI Buildout, 70 New Reactors, and $80B U.S. Funding Drive $150 Forecast
snippet: Uranium spot prices have reclaimed $100/lb as Sprott added over 4 million pounds to its physical fund, 70 new reactors are under construction globally, and the U.S. committed $80 billion to domestic reactor construction. With Kazatomprom projecting a 21-million-pound deficit by 2030, analysts see a credible path to $135–$150/lb if mine supply fails to respond.

headline: GoldSeek COT May 8: Speculators Trim Gold Longs Near $4,700 as Silver Positioning Stays Elevated
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Commitments of Traders analysis shows speculative long positions in gold futures trimming modestly as the metal consolidates near $4,700, while silver speculative positioning remains elevated heading into a sustained deficit-driven buying environment. The report also flags USDX positioning as a leading indicator for the next directional precious metals move.

headline: GOLDEN AGE: Gold Miners at 70% Margins Near $4,700 — Yet Still Trading Below Historical P/NAV
snippet: With gold near $4,700 and majors like Agnico Eagle reporting AISC of $1,483/oz against a $4,861 realized gold price in Q1, producers are generating margins approaching 70% — yet gold equities continue to trade at discounts to historical P/NAV multiples. Analysts argue the sector remains structurally undervalued as institutional money stays underweight mining.
